Add a fitted trend to a scatter or line chart

pv_trend.Rd

Fits a smooth curve ("loess", the default) or a straight regression line ("lm") through the chart's points and overlays it, with a shaded confidence ribbon. The model runs in R via stats::loess() or stats::lm(); the chart only receives ~80 fitted points, evenly spaced across the x range.

Usage

pv_trend(w, method = c("loess", "lm"), level = 0.95, slot = 2, span = 0.75)

Arguments

w

A polyviz scatter or line chart.

method

"loess" (default) for a local smoother, "lm" for a straight least-squares line.

level

Confidence level for the ribbon (default 0.95). NA drops the ribbon and draws the fitted line alone.

slot

Which palette slot colours the trend (default 2, so it contrasts with data drawn in slot 1).

span

The loess smoothing span (default 0.75); larger is smoother. Ignored by "lm".

Value

The chart, with the fitted trend attached - ready for more pipe steps.

Details

Works on scatter charts and on line charts with a numeric or date x axis. The fit pools every point into one curve, so multi-series charts are refused - facet instead: build one chart per series level and trend each. Repeated calls append, so a chart can carry a loess curve and a straight line at once.

Examples

f25 <- subset(pv_fiscal, year == 2025)
pv_scatter(f25, x = "resource_index", y = "equalization_chf") |>
  pv_trend("loess")


daily <- aggregate(revenue ~ date, pv_sales, sum)
pv_line(daily, x = "date", y = "revenue") |>
  pv_trend("lm", level = NA)
